sources.title: Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The September 22 launch names the exact GPT-6 Luna API model and says Sol/Luna were trained with methods similar to Astra. It provides no nominal total or active parameter count and does not identify Luna as a size-preserving variant of a counted base model.

sources.title: GPT-6 Luna API model reference
sources.evidence: Fresh exact-model reference lists the undated gpt-6-luna snapshot, 1,050,000 context, 922,000 maximum input and 128,000 maximum output; text/image input and text output; reasoning effort none, low, medium(default), high, xhigh and max. Function calling works in Responses; Chat Completions permits it only at none reasoning effort. Re-fetched October 27 through official documentation; the full exact-model specification supplies neither total nor active parameter counts.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: September 22 explicitly releases gpt-6-luna. September 25 records an image-encoding fix for API/Codex. October 7 updates chat-latest separately. Decisions API support for Luna began in beta October 6 and became generally available October 22; October 15 voice delegation does not establish native Luna audio input.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra System Card — September 22 Sol/Luna appendix
sources.evidence: October 27 re-audit searched the full extracted text of the original 175-page PDF fetched HTTP 200 at 15:42 UTC, and read Appendix A training and comparison sections, printed pages 119 onward. A.1 establishes the same types of data and training as Astra, not named counted-base lineage. Tables 23-29 and subsequent Luna comparisons report safety/health/capability metrics, not total or activated parameters. Full-text searches for parameter, active-count and structural terms found no count disclosure.

sources.title: GPT-6.1 Sol System Card
sources.evidence: October 27 re-audit searched the full text and read training/comparison sections of the original 48-page PDF fetched HTTP 200 at 15:42 UTC. September 29 section 2, Table 7 HealthBench and Table 12 biological-capability comparisons identify GPT-6 Luna but report scores, response lengths and evaluation metrics. Neither total nor active parameter figures are supplied; comparison values may reflect later versions.

sources.title: GPT-6.1 Terra System Card
sources.evidence: October 27 re-audit searched the full text and read training/comparison sections of the original 36-page PDF fetched HTTP 200 at 15:42 UTC and reopened its live PDF. October 26 section 2 and exact gpt-6-luna comparison columns, including section 9.0.1.1 Multimodal Troubleshooting Virology, supply evaluation scores rather than parameter sizes. No explicit total/activated-parameter column or count was found in the full text or reviewed tables.

sources.title: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna: October 2026 update
sources.evidence: October 27 re-audit searched the full text and read training/comparison sections of the original 24-page PDF fetched HTTP 200 at 15:42 UTC. The October 7 introduction distinguishes new ChatGPT versions from September versions retained in Work/Codex. Section 2 and comparison tables disclose no total or active count. The update does not establish that the production gpt-6-luna API alias switched to the October ChatGPT version.

sources.title: Prompt caching
sources.evidence: Current guide covers GPT-5.6-and-later cache controls and describes reusable KV tensors. Exact Luna reference lists prompt caching, but KV terminology does not explicitly identify Luna as Transformer or disclose dense/MoE topology.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Archived recipe explains Transformer attention but explicitly applies only to models before GPT-5.6. Its architecture description is not transferred to GPT-6 Luna.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Vision-capable models receive PDFs as extracted text and page images. Combined with exact Luna vision and endpoint support, this establishes PDF as an API document input format, not an additional native sensory modality.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Service access is limited and nonexclusive; section 9.1 reserves service intellectual property and transfers no ownership rights. With hosted distribution this supports a descriptive Proprietary classification, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: OpenAI model inventory
sources.evidence: Lists hosted GPT-6 Luna separately from the explicitly open-weight gpt-oss models. No Luna checkpoint or open-weight distribution is offered in the reviewed inventory or launch materials.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: Exact gpt-6-luna matches identify it as a replacement for older models, not a model with a listed shutdown date. This is a documentation check, not an endpoint execution test.

sources.title: EU AI Act model training-summary directory
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The current directory links GPT-5.6 Luna and GPT-6 Astra training summaries, but no exact GPT-6 Luna summary. Model-specific training quantities are not transferable Luna parameter specifications.

sources.title: Models.dev GPT-6 Luna record
sources.evidence: The baseline lead was accessed through the raw file. Its specifications and September 22 date were checked against primary sources; its promotional description and cross-generation family are corrected.

sources.title: A model guide for the GPT-6 family
sources.evidence: October 2 guide reopened October 27. The exact GPT-6 Luna entry and model/effort/speed comparisons describe workloads, prices and serving controls, with no parameter counts or counted-base lineage. Cost and speed tiers are not parameter specifications.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra public summary of training content
sources.evidence: Original summary fetched HTTP 200 October 27 at 15:42 UTC and read for this re-audit. Section 1.2 identifies GPT-6 Astra, not GPT-6 Luna; section 1.3 reports training-data quantities, including token and image ranges. It supplies no Luna total/active count or named counted-base relationship.

family.note: Normalize to the GPT-6 generation; Luna is a capability tier across generations.

release_date.note: Explicit public/API release date. September 3 is the original Astra card date, not the later-added Luna appendix release. October ChatGPT variants are separate.

open_weights.note: Documented distribution is hosted API/Work/Codex; no Luna weights are offered in the reviewed release or inventory.

license.note: Descriptive classification of hosted model access under service terms, not an SPDX checkpoint license.

parameters_b.note: October 27 parameter-only re-audit: no nominal total count in the original Luna release/appendix, exact API reference, later Sol/Terra comparisons or current guide. Bounded fresh exact-name searches for parameter counts, billion/trillion figures and original technical reports found no supported new specification. Similar training methods to Astra do not establish a counted-base lineage; training-data volumes, performance estimates and another generation's Luna assumptions are not literal parameters.

active_parameters_b.note: October 27 independent active-count recheck found no published nominal activated-parameter figure for exact GPT-6 Luna. Later OpenAI research comparisons were checked explicitly: Sol 6.1 Tables 7/12 and Terra 6.1 section 9.0.1.1 give scores/lengths, not active-count columns. Fresh exact-name active/activated-parameter searches produced no original model-team count. Neither a dense assumption nor total=active inference is justified.

architecture.note: Exact-model training, comparison and targeted architecture/interpretability searches did not establish production topology. KV caching alone is insufficient, and the older Transformer recipe explicitly excludes this generation. Similar training methods to Astra do not prove architectural identity.

context_window.note: Exact current API total context; maximum input 922,000 and maximum output 128,000 tokens are explicitly listed. Product chat limits are separate.

modalities.note: Native API input is text/image and output is text. PDF is retained as an API format converted to text/page images. Hosted image-generation tools and GPT-Live delegation do not establish native image output or audio input.

reasoning.note: Reasoning tokens supported; efforts none, low, medium(default), high, xhigh and max. Optional none does not negate reasoning capability.

tool_call.note: Responses supports built-in tools and function calling. Exact model reference also permits function calling in Chat Completions only with reasoning_effort=none; the Astra Responses-only restriction is not transferred.

description.value: GPT-6 reasoning model for focused, high-volume tasks, with text and image input and tool calling.
description.note: Replace comparative efficiency promotion with documented purpose and capabilities.

patch.notes: Released September 22, 2026 in the API, Work and Codex. The model reference lists only the undated gpt-6-luna identifier, not an immutable dated snapshot. Current API limits are 1,050,000 context, 922,000 input and 128,000 output tokens. Reasoning supports none through max with medium as default. Use Responses for built-in tools; Chat Completions function calling requires reasoning_effort=none. PDF denotes API extraction into text/page images. September 25 fixed image encoding; the October ChatGPT versions are separately identified in their system card and are not assumed to replace the production API model. Decisions API support was added October 6 and became generally available October 22. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed; shared training methods with Astra do not establish a counted base. Architecture remains unverified. No Luna shutdown date was found; endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains null/undisclosed total and active counts after reopening the original release, API reference, full September appendix, later Sol/Terra and October cards, current model guide and training-summary directory. No supported nominal count or counted-base lineage was found. Explicit parameter patch values are null; the other 12 field assessments are unchanged.
